chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a woman whose husband died before consummating the marriage with her, saying: 'She shall not marry until she completes a waiting period of four months and ten days, which is the waiting period for a woman whose husband has died.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.الْمُتَوَفَّى عَنْهَا: The one who died while she was his wife
key_terms.يَمْسَهَا: To consummate the marriage (literally: to touch her)

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a woman whose husband dies before consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's chain in al-Istibsar clarifies a key juristic distinction: despite the absence of physical consummation (dakhil), the widow observes the full four-month and ten-day 'iddah, mirroring the ruling for consummated marriages. This ruling underscores the principle that the primary purpose of this waiting period is to ascertain potential pregnancy and honor the marital bond, rather than merely confirming conception. It highlights the consistency of Imam Ali’s legal reasoning in establishing clear, uniform standards for widows regardless of the marriage's physical completion.
